prompt: Let $A$ be a set and $R\subseteq A\times A$ a binary relation on $A$. Define $\Delta_A=\{(x,x):x\in A\}$ and the inverse relation $R^{-1}=\{(y,x):(x,y)\in R\}$. Which condition is equivalent to $R$ being both symmetric and antisymmetric?

answers.explanation: Symmetry supplies the reverse of each pair; antisymmetry then makes its endpoints equal. Any subset of the diagonal satisfies both.
The empty relation works, but nonempty subsets of the diagonal also work.
On at least two elements, the universal relation violates antisymmetry.
Excluding loops does not exclude off-diagonal pairs.
All loops are not required: a proper subset of the diagonal also works.
Reflexivity permits off-diagonal pairs that can violate one of the required properties.
This expresses only symmetry; two-way pairs between distinct elements may remain.
This expresses asymmetry and permits one-way off-diagonal pairs.
This expresses only antisymmetry; an off-diagonal one-way pair is permitted.
This forces every loop to be present as well; the requested condition allows missing loops.
